Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning information about the county-based system of collecting legal financial obligations.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to information about legal financial obligations;amending RCW 36.23.110; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that legal financialobligations can be a significant problem for people trying to satisfycriminal penalties. Further, the countybased system of collectinglegal financial obligations makes it difficult to ascertain both howsuccessful people are in satisfying these obligations and how manypeople fail to satisfy these obligations. Therefore, the legislatureintends to collect the information necessary to ascertain the successand efficiency of the countybased system of collecting legal financialobligations by changing the form of the annual report required to besubmitted to the legislature.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 36.23.110 and 2003 c 379 s 20 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The Washington association of county officials, in consultationwith county clerks, shall determine a funding formula for allocation ofmoneys to counties for purposes of collecting legal financial p. 1 HB 1569obligations, and report this formula to the legislature and theadministrative office of the courts by September 1, 2003. TheWashington association of county officials shall report on: (1) The amounts of legal financial obligations collected by each ofthe county clerks; (2) The number of individuals, by county, owing legal financialobligations; (3) The total amount of outstanding debt from the individuals insubsection (2) of this section; (4) The amount of outstanding legal financial obligation debt fromrestitution; (5) The amount of outstanding legal financial obligation debt fromfines and fees; (6) The amount of outstanding legal financial obligation debt fromcollections costs, including interest and clerks fees; (7) The number of cases of people making regular payments."Regular payments" is defined as payments that are less than sixty dayspast due; (8) The number of notices of delinquency sent out; (9) The number of individuals sent notices of delinquency; (10) The number of notices to appear for nonpayment issued; (11) The number of individuals sent notices for nonpayment; (12) The number of individuals whose wages were garnisheed; (13) The number of tax refunds intercepted; (14) The number of individuals issued property tax liens; (15) The number of warrants for failure to appear issued; (16) The number of individuals for whom warrants were issued; (17) The total number of outstanding warrants for failure toappear; (18) The total number of outstanding warrants for nonpayment; (19) The number of people jailed for failure to appear; (20) The number of people jailed for nonpayment; and (21) The average number of days spent in jail for nonpayment.The report shall be submitted to the appropriate committees of thelegislature no later than December 1, ((2004)) 2013, and annuallythereafter.
